# [TASK] TMDB-shaped person endpoints with read-through/save-through (actor-service)

## Task
Extend actor-service (#18) with TMDB v3-shaped person endpoints, read-through/save-through against PostgreSQL, so the React app's actor pages can call them directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `GET /person/{id}`, `/person/{id}/movie_credits`, `/person/{id}/images`, `/person/popular`, `/search/person` implemented (`PersonFacadeController`; `PersonFacadeControllerTest`); `discover/movie?with_cast=` delegated to movie-service per ADR-002 (movie-list data belongs there, not actor-service)
- [x] Read-through/save-through against the persisted `actors` table, rate-limited to TMDB's published 40 requests/10s (`TmdbRateLimitInterceptor`, Bucket4j; `TmdbRateLimitInterceptorTest`)
- [x] 12 of 13 comparable fields match real TMDB output field-for-field; `deathday` is intentionally not modeled since the React app never reads it (manual: `GET /person/{id}` against the live TMDB API, diff the JSON against this service's response)
- [x] A repeat request for the same person is served from PostgreSQL, not TMDB (`ActorServiceIntegrationTest`, "Facade /person/{id}/images: TMDB-shaped, persisted, second call hits no TMDB")
- [x] Full controller → service → PostgreSQL → TMDB stack is green (`ActorServiceIntegrationTest`, Testcontainers + WireMock)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 9

## Notes
Original spec required lossless round-trip of TMDB JSON — superseded by ADR-010 (typed, mapped catalog instead of raw passthrough). Only consequence: `deathday` isn't stored; no consumer reads it.

Audit #274: `:backend:actor-service:test` could not be run this session — no Java 25 toolchain in this sandbox (see #31's Notes). Test names above were confirmed by reading the test source.
